sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Beverwijk, in Noord-Holland, charges for parking in its centre with a free first hour and has long wanted parking use to be fairer between the centre and the Bazaar area. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 20 November 2025: on-street parking costs 1.70 euros per 60 minutes in both the Centrum and the Bazaar zones, with the first 60 minutes free in Centrum when the plate is registered at a machine or by phone, a daily maximum of 14.30 euros in Centrum and none at the Bazaar, and a penalty of 82.00 euros [0]. The 2025 rates were 1.65 euros an hour and 14.00 euros for the daily maximum, with the Bazaar charged from the first hour [1]. Under the 2025 designation, paid hours in Centrum run Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 19:00, in the area around the Kennemer Theater until 22:00, and at the Bazaar on Saturdays, Sundays and named holidays from 07:00 to 18:00; we did not find a 2026 designation, so the 2026 hours are unconfirmed [2]. At most two resident permits are allowed per address in the centre, and residents of new-build projects in the Spoorzone, where parking is arranged on private land, are excluded; in 2026 a first resident permit costs 28.47 euros and a second 91.12 euros [3]. The council adopted a new parking-standards note in October 2023, dropping the exemption for small developments, giving the Spoorzone lower norms and setting 5,000 euros per space for using spare capacity in the centre [4]. In September 2023 five parties tabled an amendment on paid parking to 19:00 and a reduced Saturday tariff, and we did not find the vote [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The questions about new parking are open. A 2022 survey reported to the council in April 2023 found the busiest moment in the centre on Saturday between 14:00 and 16:00, at 78 percent average occupancy, against the council's 85 percent maximum, with centre-wide Saturday-afternoon occupancy of 78 to 84 percent from 2019 to 2022 [6]. A consultancy note of August 2023 named the NS park-and-ride at Wijckermolen, the Meerplein, Halve Maan and Wijckerpoort as search locations for a future stacked car park, assuming 75 spaces at the Slangenwegje would go around 2024 to 2025 and the 448 public Meerplein spaces from about 2027; that is a planning assumption and not a decision [12]. Samen Lokaal said in a committee of September 2023 that it wanted an above-ground car park near the centre, a party position [13]. A proposal of September 2024 asked for 94,053 euros for new pay machines and for information columns at the car parks Halve Maan, Beverplein, Meerplein and Wijckerpoort able to take a guidance system, which was to be studied in 2025 [10]. A licence-plate scan car began testing on 23 May 2024, with official use in the centre planned from 25 June 2024 [11]. On charging, a traffic decision of 4 June 2026 reserves two spaces at each charge point listed in an annex, and rules of April 2026 allow a charge cable of at most 5 metres over the pavement to a public space between 20:00 and 16:00 for people without private parking [14][15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The 2022 survey found that of all parked vehicles 52 percent had neither a permit nor paid, 80 percent on the Meerplein, because centre parking was free on Saturdays then, and that the edge car parks behaved unevenly, with Wijckerpoort averaging 23 percent but reaching 98 percent on a Thursday afternoon [6][8]. It found the NS park-and-ride at the station peaking at only 6 percent occupancy [7]. The Beverwijkse Bazaar runs its own car parks P0, P1, P3, P4 and P5, where weekend parking costs at most 5 euros a car a day, with 16 charge points on P4, and the page gives no capacities [16].

Our data cover the P+R Wijckermolen, with 121 spaces, for about 56 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 8% on weekdays and 3% at weekends, and peaked at 33% around midday on a Tuesday, so it is still almost empty, as in the 2022 survey. We found no source naming who operates it beyond the NS site owner, and the other car parks in the centre are not in our data.
